entries.1e4618f750bef25a: Under its 3-year medium-term management plan ‘Yokohama Transformation 2026 (YX2026),’ covering 2024 to 2026, it states that it will advance ‘deepening’ to strengthen the strengths of existing businesses and ‘exploration’ to seek new value, and carry out the final phase of its transformation. In consumer tires, it is raising the share of high value-added products and, as part of building a low-cost, high-efficiency production system, is taking on the challenge of the ‘1-year factory’ concept of launching a factory within 1 year. In the OHT business, it aims to strengthen its market position through a multi-brand strategy and, drawing on the OTR business of Goodyear acquired in February 2025, to expand sales channels and production capacity for tires for construction and mining vehicles. In the MB business, it states that it will advance the restructuring of the value chain in the hose piping business and reform of the production structure in North America.

entries.451435bbbf03f2a0: It states that it holds the top share in tires for agricultural and forestry machinery, which are forecast to account for about 40% of the OHT market, and holds a 2nd-place share in tires for industrial and port vehicles, which are forecast to account for 25% of the market.
entries.479b90838fbc4ddb: In the OHT business, it states that it will strengthen its market position through its ‘multi-brand strategy,’ which draws on the production, sales and technology strengths it holds at each tier from Tier1 to Tier3. In tires for agricultural machinery, it is expanding sales mainly under the Mitas, Alliance and Galaxy brands. In tires for industrial and port vehicles, it aims to expand the areas where it offers its ‘Interfit’ tire maintenance service, provided by specialist staff.
entries.4a2f03a1234b3fdf: Tires are divided into two categories by sales destination: new-vehicle tires supplied to automakers, and replacement tires sold when vehicle owners replace their tires. New-vehicle tires exceeded the prior year, due to the expansion of new models supplied in Japan and the winning of original equipment fitment on premium cars, mainly SUV and CUV models, in Europe and North America. Replacement tires exceeded the prior year as sales of high value-added products grew, driven by careful sales activities in Japan, focus on high-inch products (large-size tires) in European countries, and strengthened sales of on-road SUV and CUV tires in North America. The company cites ADVAN and GEOLANDAR, along with winter tires, as high value-added products. Revenue for this category is not separately disclosed.
entries.4a8666beacc33ae0: This business involves rubber and resin products other than tires. It manufactures and sells conveyor belts, various hoses, fenders (members that cushion the impact when ships berth at quays), oil fences, marine hoses and aviation parts. Manufacturing and sales are carried out by the company as well as by Yokohama Industries Americas Inc., Yokohama Industries Americas Ohio Inc., Xieji Gongye Gufen Youxian Gongsi, Yokohama Rubber (Thailand) Co., Ltd., Hangzhou Youkehaoma Xiangjiao Zhipin Youxian Gongsi, companies in Mexico and Indonesia, Shandong Yokohama Xiangjiao Gongye Zhipin Youxian Gongsi and others, while sales are handled by Yokohama Rubber MB Japan Co., Ltd., Shanghai Youkehaoma Xiangjiao Zhipin Shangmao Youxian Gongsi, Yokohama Aerospace America Inc. and others. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥105,552 million (up 0.3% year on year), accounting for 8.5% of consolidated revenue. The company explains that the Hose and Piping Business exceeded the prior year, as demand from North American automakers rose despite lower demand from domestic construction machinery makers, and that the Industrial Materials Business exceeded the prior year, owing to stable orders for conveyor belts, strong demand for marine products and increased orders for defense equipment.
entries.523b069fa9f2c92b: This category covers conveyor belts, marine products and others. Revenue exceeded the prior year due to stable orders for conveyor belts, capture of strong demand for marine products, and increased orders for defense equipment. Revenue for this category is not separately disclosed.
entries.525cb354fcf72075: In the tire business, it makes various tires, including those for passenger cars, trucks and buses, light trucks, agricultural machinery, industrial vehicles, mining and construction vehicles, and forestry machinery, as well as tubes, aluminum wheels and automotive-related products. In the MB business, it makes conveyor belts, various hoses, fenders, oil fences, marine hoses and aviation parts. Other businesses include sporting goods and information processing services. Except for a small portion, all production is make-to-stock.
entries.608f98fdf4901862: It states that it holds the top share in tires for agricultural and forestry machinery, which are forecast to account for about 40% of the OHT market, and holds a 2nd-place share in tires for industrial and port vehicles, which are forecast to account for 25% of the market. In tires for construction and mining vehicles, its share remains small, and in February 2025 it acquired Goodyear’s OTR business.

entries.b7be5dd6087b4246: Revenue for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥1,234,959 million, up 12.8% from the previous year. The consolidated financial statements are prepared in accordance with [[term:ifrs|IFRS]]. Revenue from external customers was ¥1,121,284 million for tires (90.8% of consolidated revenue), ¥105,552 million for MB (8.5%) and ¥8,123 million for other businesses. Tire revenue increased due to growth in sales of high value-added products and the addition of the results of Goodyear’s OTR business, acquired in February 2025. MB revenue exceeded the previous year, reflecting higher demand from North American automakers in the hose piping business, stable orders for conveyor belts and higher orders for defense equipment in the industrial materials business, among other factors.

entries.e5467c88b8d68512: It is the core business of the company group, manufacturing and selling tires for passenger cars, trucks and buses, agricultural machinery, and mining and construction vehicles, as well as automotive accessories such as aluminum wheels. Product categories are various tires for passenger cars, trucks and buses, small trucks, agricultural machinery, industrial vehicles, mining and construction vehicles, and forestry machinery, as well as tubes, aluminum wheels and automotive accessories. Manufacturing and sales are carried out by the company as well as by Aichi Tire Kogyo Co., Ltd., Nihon Giant Tire Co., Ltd., the retread tire company Yokohama Tire Retread Co., Ltd., manufacturing companies in the Philippines, Thailand, Russia, the United States (Mississippi and Virginia), Vietnam, India and China (Hangzhou and Suzhou), Alliance Tire Company Ltd., Yokohama TWS S.p.A. and others. On the sales side, domestic sales companies include Yokohama Tire Japan Co., Ltd. and others, and overseas sales companies include Yokohama Tire Corporation and others. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥1,121,284 million (up 14.3% year on year), accounting for 90.8% of consolidated revenue; this is the largest business. The company explains that revenue exceeded the prior year due to growth in sales of high value-added products and the addition of the results of the OTR business of Goodyear, acquired in February 2025.
entries.f04a2b74f7b84763: For the fiscal year ended December 2025, [[term:net-income-attributable-to-owners-of-parent|profit attributable to owners of the parent]] was ¥105,398 million, up 40.7% from the previous year.
